open_items: ILO blanket-403 provider_down episode: eleventh occurrence, started cycle 442, resolved by cycle 443 (one cycle), confirmed still healthy through cycle 469. Matches the usual one-to-two-cycle resolution pattern (244, 251, 260, 264, 272, 281, 321, 382, 412); only the ninth occurrence (cycles 396-411) ran long, escalating to a standing block at the ~24h/12-cycle mark. No cause has ever been confirmed for any occurrence; ILO gives no public status signal. Watch for a twelfth occurrence.

IMF provider_down flap: first occurrence, cycle 419 (gateway metadata 503, gateway data 503, direct metadata 503, direct data ReadTimeout, all at once), resolved by cycle 420. Confirmed with a live recheck at 2026-08-29T06:44Z (direct metadata HTTP 200). Distinct from the cycle 161 references:* 401 contract flap below. Watch for a second occurrence.

ILO contract-only blanket 403 (new shape): cycle 418, all nine non-ignored ILO contract assertions (auth:listing, constraint:availableconstraint, errors:missing_artefact, six of the eight references:* variants) flipped to HTTP 403 / verdict broken in the same cycle, while all five basic checks (gateway+direct metadata/data/json) stayed ok:true. Derived status healthy -> degraded, not provider_down (the 396-411 blanket-403 episode failed the basic checks too). Live recheck at 2026-08-29T00:44Z: all affected URLs back to 200 (or the expected 500/404), roughly 43 minutes after the cycle started. First occurrence of this exact shape. No second occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a second occurrence; if it recurs or widens to the basic checks, treat as part of the existing recurring ILO block family rather than a separate bug.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: twenty-fifth occurrence, cycle 403, resolved by cycle 404, healthy through cycle 469. Consistent with the long-running one-cycle-flap pattern (the gateway's own 60s call deadline firing under a slow response), not a new bug. Standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result in monitor/checks_gateway.py) remains open as a code-change-scope fix, not actioned by this read-only routine.

ILO gateway_issue, both gateway metadata and gateway data HTTP 403 together, direct healthy: first occurrence of this exact combination, cycle 384, resolved by cycle 385. Distinct from the gateway-data-only flap (cycles 322, 370, metadata still passing) and from the gateway-metadata-500 episode (cycles 268-269, HTTP 500 not 403, data still passing). No second occurrence through cycle 469 outside of the cycle 454 blanket episode (see above, a different and broader shape). Watch for a second occurrence of this specific shape.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: eleventh occurrence, cycle 381, resolved by cycle 382. All eleven occurrences have now resolved within one cycle. Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py).

ILO gateway-data-only 403 flap (standalone): two occurrences on record, cycle 370 (resolved by 371) and cycle 322 (tail end of the cycle 321 blanket-403 episode). Both resolved within one to two cycles. No new occurrence through cycle 469 of this specific standalone shape (the cycle 384, 396-411, and 442 episodes are the broader both-metadata-and-data or blanket shapes, see above). Watch for a third occurrence of this standalone data-only shape.

SBS gateway DNS resolution flap: first occurrence, cycle 366 (`Temporary failure in name resolution` on gateway metadata, gateway data probe timed out), resolved by cycle 367. No second occurrence through cycle 469. Isolated to SBS; same failure shape previously seen for FBOS at cycle 50 (treated as infrastructure, not provider-down). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate if it recurs.

UNICEF HTTP 429 flap: eighth occurrence cycle 430 (gateway data and direct data+json all HTTP 429, both metadata checks ok), confirmed resolved by cycle 431 and stable healthy through cycle 469. Live recheck at 2026-08-30T06:43Z: direct data and metadata both HTTP 200. Prior occurrences cycle 126, 178, 262, 305, 346, all resolved within one cycle; this one matches the pattern. Watch for a ninth occurrence.

ABS and ESTAT gateway_issue coincided in the same cycle twice now (cycle 319 and cycle 389, both resolved within one cycle). No third same-cycle occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a third same-cycle occurrence with matching failure text.

OECD gateway_issue 403 Forbidden episode (cycles 290-292, gateway list_dataflows and gateway data probe both HTTP 403, direct path healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 293. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a second occurrence; escalate for real if a future episode again spans more than one cycle.

ILO direct-path 403 flap (basic checks): tenth occurrence cycle 286, resolved by cycle 287 (one cycle, as usual), clean since (superseded by the blanket 403 pattern, a different and more severe pattern -- see above). Prior occurrences cycle 32, 94, 159, 166, 202, 238, 244, 249, 267. Watch for an eleventh occurrence of this specific direct-only shape.

ILO references:contentconstraint broken (500) at cycle 274 resolved by cycle 275 (reads `ignored`, not `broken`, in the current cycle's contract rows). Second occurrence overall of this assertion flapping (first was a same-cycle blip at cycle 199). No new occurrence through cycle 469 outside of the blanket-403 episodes (see above), which read all ILO assertions as `broken` for a different reason. Watch for a third occurrence of the 500-specific flap.

ILO gateway_issue episode (cycles 268-269, gateway metadata HTTP 500 on list_dataflows, direct healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 270. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Distinct pattern from the cycle 322, 370, 384, and 396-411/442 gateway data/metadata 403 episodes (see above): different HTTP status (500 vs 403). Watch separately.

ECB contract-probe 504 flap (second pattern): constraint:availableconstraint (504 -> 404) and references:none (504 -> 200) both showed a was/now change in /api/contracts between cycle 283 and 286, verdict stayed ok throughout. No further changes list entries on these assertions through cycle 469. Not the same assertions as the cycles 182-183 references:* 504 flap (that watch item is separate, still clean). Watch for recurrence on these two assertions specifically.
ABS contract 503 flap: dialect:sdmx3 and errors:missing_artefact both returned 503 at cycle 234 only, resolved by cycle 235. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a second occurrence.
ECB metadata 503 (provider_down): occurred cycle 199 only, resolved by cycle 200. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a second occurrence.
ABS gateway metadata 502 Bad Gateway flap: occurred cycle 198 only, resolved by cycle 199. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for recurrence. Distinct from the empty-error-body flap above.
UNICEF direct-path HTTP 404 'no data found' flap: occurred cycle 197 only, resolved by cycle 198. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a second occurrence.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 469: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes. Latest occurrence: ABS encoding:structure_xml, cycle 469.
IMF references:* 401 flap: first and only occurrence, cycle 161, resolved by cycle 162. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a second occurrence.
ECB references:* 504 flap (cycles 182-183 pattern): first occurrence, cycles 182-183, resolved by cycle 184. No new occurrence through cycle 469. Watch for a second occurrence.
